plate.viewWhy: The level torso, the bar path from floor to chest and the back-angle fault all happen front-to-back (c2, c4, c6); the census draws it side, like the parent.
plate.equipment: Straight barbell with plates resting on the floor line under the shoulders at the start (c1, c3).
plate.start: Hips hinged a little higher than a deadlift (c1), torso parallel to the floor with shoulders and hips level (c2), knees slightly bent, feet about shoulder width (c10), arms straight down to the bar on the floor (c3).
plate.end: Same torso and hip angle (c4); bar touching the base of the chest or abs (c4, c5).

checkpoints.what: Torso level with the floor, shoulders and hips at the same height.

checkpoints.label: Torso still
checkpoints.what: Only the bar and arms move; no standing up to pull.

mistake.what: Back angle rises: the lifter stands partly up to yank the bar.
mistake.why: Named as a common fault and a sign of too much weight (c6); it turns a strict row into a heave on a lift that loads the lower back (c18).

tells.text: Bar rests on the floor each rep
Back stays level as the bar rises

grip.handContact: Bar across the base of the fingers and top of the palm (pull archetype); straps allowed when the grip gives out first.
grip.wrist: Bent back into its natural grip position (about 35 degrees), not curled forward; grip weakens when the wrist moves away from it.

setup.step: New to lifting? Start with seated or chest-supported rows first.
Bar on the floor; stand over it with feet about shoulder width.
Hinge with the hips a little higher than a deadlift; grip overhand, slightly wider than the shoulders.
Can’t reach it with a flat back? Raise the bar on blocks or plates.
Learn it with a light weight; add 2-10% once you beat your target reps by one or two.

posture.point: Torso level, shoulders and hips at the same height.
Upper body still; only the bar and arms move.
Shoulders not shrugged; hips don’t come forward.
Both feet flat the whole set.
Set the bar down at a dead stop each rep.

handlingMistakes.mistake: Standing partly up to yank the bar.
handlingMistakes.fix: Use less weight and keep the torso level.
Raise the bar on blocks or plates until you can grip it with a flat back.

handlingMistakes.mistake: Elbows flared wide to the sides.
handlingMistakes.fix: Lighten the load; pull the bar toward the hips.
